Prompt referral

Avoid repeating key steps like returning to GP for referral or re assessment or investigations.

Self-referral is accepted.

Assessment within 1 week of request.

Abortion within 1 week of assessment.

Blood test = not routinely required, blood group is needed if >12weeks.

LMWH for 7 days

Contraindication of Medical Abortion:

Suspected or known ectopic.

Allergy to misoprostol or Mifepristone.

Severe uncontrolled asthma.

Chronic adrenal failure

Inherited porphyria

Extra consideration of Medical Abortion;

Long term steroid therapy

because mifepristone can exacerbate underlying conditions as it is a glucocorticoid receptor antagonist.

On anticoagulants

Risk of bleeding – so should be stopped before abortion and started again after procedure.

Bleeding disorders

Need clinical setting.

Symptomatic anemia.

Need hospital setting

IUD in place.

IUD should ideally be removed in advance of treatment if not retrieved then confirm its presence by X – ray abdomen.

Contraindication of surgical Abortion

Where pregnancy cannot be removed through cervix.

Extra consideration of Surgical Abortion.

Bleeding disorders.

Abnormal placentation.

Use of anti-coagulants

Severe cardiopulmonary disease.

Very high BMI

Distorted uterine cavity by fibroids or any other anomaly.

Previous cervical surgery.

Type 3 FGM.

These cases need extra care like use of special instruments, type of Anaesthesia, ultrasound and guidance.

Pain Management for Medical Abortion:

Should be given always

NSAIDS – either prophylactic or at time of cramping.

Non – pharmacological – hot water, heat pads.

Narcotic analgesics if pain is more especially in higher gestation.

Surgical Abortion:

Before 14 weeks:

Vacuum aspiration either

Electric vacuum aspiration EVA

Manual vacuum aspiration MVA

MVA accommodate 4 – 12mm cannula.

All products should be inspected after evacuation.

12 – 14 weeks:

Dilatation and evacuation D & E.

D & E require cervical preparation using dilators or pharmacological agents, skilled, experienced care provider.

Vacuum aspiration can be done up till 16 weeks using large cannula 16mm.

D & C (dilation and curettage) is an obsolete method.

Cervix preparation reduces risk of incomplete abortion.

Pain Management for Surgical TOP:

Analgesia should always be offered:

Most of the times:

NSAIDS

Local anesthesia + Verbal reassurance

Conscious sedation

General Anesthesia:

Not recommended routinely, if considered then use I/V propofol and fentanyl rather inhalational agents.

Local anesthesia:

Lidocaine as Para cervical block can be used to alleviate discomfort from cervical dilatation and uterine evacuation.

Conscious Sedation:

Should be offered with local anesthesia if available.
